title: Open Worship App question corpus
description: One file per PAGE of the app. `questions.mjs` reads every *.json in this directory except this one, so adding a page is adding a file. Every question must be answerable from the recipe or the tools it names -- a suggestion the assistant cannot answer is worse than no suggestion.

page.description: Stable id, and the first part of every question id in the file.

label.description: What a user would call this page.

window.description: The window it lives in, e.g. "reader.html". Null when it is not one window.

focus.description: Which window of the app it belongs to, named by that page's html base name -- the same keys `botFocus.mjs` declares, because the key is spliced into `page: "<key>.html"` by the tools. A LIST when one page belongs to several: the slide editor is a tab of the main window, so its questions answer from the Presenter too. Null means EVERY window -- settings and the find bar read the same wherever they are asked from.

updated.description: ISO date of the last content change, bumped whenever a question is added, reworded or removed.

id.description: Unique within the file; the middle part of a question id.

label.description: Shown beside a suggestion, so it must say WHICH of several right answers is theirs.

panel.description: The panel it lives in, as `data-widget-name` spells it.

recipes.description: The manual recipes this whole section is drawn from.

focusKey.description: A window of the app, by its html base name. Declared once in `botFocus.mjs`; `questions.test.mjs` fails on a page file naming one that is not there.

recipeId.description: A manual recipe id, the same one `owa_help_search` and `owa_help_page` use.

id.description: Unique within the section. STABLE: a scoreboard row and a regression test may name it, so reword `text` freely and leave this alone.

text.description: The question as a volunteer would type it, ending in a question mark. No file paths, ids or code names -- the person asking is running a service, not reading the source.

kind.description: `state` and `fix` are the ones that need the live app, not just the manual.

keywords.description: The words they would type INSTEAD -- what they call it, and what they say when it is going wrong. Not a restatement of `text`, which is already matched.

starter.description: May be offered as a chip in the empty window.

template.description: The chip fills the ask box instead of asking. For a question that cannot be asked as it stands because it carries a placeholder the user has to replace -- an address, a name. Pressing one is the start of typing, not the end of it.

starterRank.description: Which starters lead, lowest first. Ranks are compared ACROSS every file a focus can see, not within one file, so a rank must be unique among the pages that share a focus -- and a rank in a `focus: null` file (`common.json`, `troubleshooting.json`) competes in EVERY window at once. Leave it unset to land after every ranked one.

resources.description: Everything needed to answer it WITHOUT a search round.

find.description: The exact visible control, in `owa_find_ui` syntax -- "Background > Videos" when a bare word is ambiguous.

menu.description: A native menu path ("View → Widgets"). Use this instead of `find` for menu bar items: they are not in the DOM and cannot be ringed.

shortcut.description: The keystroke, written the way the manual writes it. Only ones the shortcut table actually lists.

tools.description: The `owa_*` tools that answer it from the live app.

guide.description: Whether a step-by-step walkthrough can be run for it.
